name: NOCO Boost X GBX75 Jump Starter
description: 2,500 amps of "you're not stranded today" in something the size of a lunchbox. It'll jump the Sprinter's diesel, charge a phone as a power bank, and the built-in light has bailed me out of more than one dark-campsite fix. The piece of gear I hope I never need — and am very glad I have.

name: Koonie 10,000mAh Clip-On Camping Fan + Lantern
description: A still, hot night in the van is the enemy of good sleep — and this little clip fan is the fix. Genuinely quiet, 360° tilt, runs all night on a charge, and doubles as a soft lantern. Clips to the bed frame, a cabinet, wherever you need the air. Small thing, huge difference.

name: SOUDFK Rechargeable Bottle Lamp
description: Pop it on an empty wine bottle and the whole van goes warm and golden. Rechargeable, a few color tones, no cords — just soft light for the quiet end of a long road day. The little luxuries are what make a small space feel like home.

name: Camco Bamboo Folding Camp Table
description: Sets up in seconds, folds flat to nothing, and the bamboo top is sturdy enough to actually cook on. Camp coffee at sunrise, dinner prep, a hand of cards after dark — this little table is where a lot of the day ends up happening.

name: DALUOBO Removable RV Table Leg
description: The trick to living small: a table that disappears. This aluminum pedestal drops in when you need a surface and lifts right out when you don't — 360° rotation, adjustable height, no tools. Floor space back in two seconds.

name: TeamObsidian Waterproof Bike Cover
description: Bikes live on the back of the van through sun, rain, and highway grit — this heavy ripstop cover keeps the weather and road off them. Reflective straps, grab handles, and it cinches down tight so it won't flap at 70. Cheap insurance for gear that isn't.

name: The MILEPOST — Alaska Travel Planner
description: If you're pointing the rig north, this is the bible. Mile-by-mile logs of every highway through Alaska, the Yukon, and BC — every pullout, fuel stop, and view worth stopping for. Published since 1949, and still the one book I wouldn't drive the North Country without.

name: Neso Gigante Portable Sun Shade
description: Shade is the difference between a good camp afternoon and a miserable one. This throws 11 feet of UPF 50+ cover, anchors with sand bags instead of stakes (so it grips any ground), shrugs off wind, and packs to a shoulder bag. Beach, desert, dry lakebed — instant shade anywhere.

name: Staying Connected
description: Internet from the middle of nowhere — Starlink plus a cell booster is what keeps me online when the nearest town is an hour away.

name: Power on the Go
description: A solid portable power station (and a little solar) is the difference between chasing hookups and camping free, off-grid, for days.

name: Clean Water
description: An inline water filter is cheap insurance — you never quite know what's coming out of that campground spigot.

name: Finding Camp
description: The apps that find free, legal places to park. I lean on these constantly — see the toolkit in my guide.

name: Outside Living
description: A good chair and an awning mat. Camp is where you actually live — make the patch of dirt outside your door feel like home.
